goal: Contain source-originated per-file failures so unaffected files still transfer without corrupting protocol framing or destroying valid destination data.
recommended_approach: Keep the proposed pre-open, same-handle validation, bounded chunk framing, explicit success/failure terminators, need ledger, and atomic staging, but make record ownership connection-specific, protect failed destination subtrees during mirror deletion, use ownership-tracked staging with bounded aggregate space, and preserve macOS clone-first behavior.
comparison: The reviewed plan has the right overall architecture and substantially addresses the root cause, but several concurrency, deletion-safety, staging-lifecycle, and fast-path details prevent it from being the best implementation as written.
material_changes: Protect the exact failed path and every descendant from the mirror deletion pass.
Identify data-plane lanes by connection or use an unforgeable per-record lease, including for every resume block and completion.
Make crash-orphan cleanup ownership-aware and safe across concurrent sessions instead of deleting by filename prefix.
Add destination-scoped byte admission for concurrent staged records so staging does not manufacture avoidable volume-full failures.
On macOS, attempt fclonefileat against an absent staging path before creating a fallback staging file.

findings.title: A skipped file can still cause its destination subtree to be deleted
findings.evidence: docs/plan/SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT.md:136 — the plan assumes retaining the failed manifest path makes mirror deletion safe, but crates/blit-core/src/mirror_planner.rs:221 retains only that exact path and its ancestors; descendants are deleted by plan_from_sets.
findings.predicted_failure: If source path `foo` is a file that becomes unreadable while destination `foo` is a directory containing `foo/bar`, the skip preserves the `foo` directory entry but mirror deletion removes `foo/bar`, destroying pre-existing destination data during a contained source failure.
findings.better_approach: Carry an uncapped exact set of failed ledger paths into mirror planning and exclude both each failed path and all component-wise descendants; add a regression with a skipped source file colliding with a populated destination directory.

findings.title: The ledger does not distinguish concurrent data-plane sockets
findings.evidence: docs/plan/SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT.md:285 — every TCP connection is represented by the same `Lane::DataPlane`, despite crates/blit-core/src/transfer_session/data_plane.rs:294 spawning multiple concurrent receive workers and crates/blit-core/src/remote/transfer/pipeline.rs:1381 accepting path-bearing block completions on each socket.
findings.predicted_failure: A malformed or buggy peer can send blocks or `BlockComplete` for a resume record activated on another socket; the same-lane check passes, allowing premature finalization, cross-socket writes, or a later session-fatal transition instead of rejecting the first misplaced record.
findings.better_approach: Use a unique lane ID such as `(epoch, socket_id)`, or return an opaque record lease from the ledger activation and require that lease for all subsequent blocks and completion.

findings.title: Prefix-based staging cleanup has no durable ownership proof
findings.evidence: docs/plan/SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT.md:584 — staging names are target-independent and the target mapping exists only in `RecordWriter`, yet lines 604-605 require a later run to remove crash orphans by their recognizable prefix.
findings.predicted_failure: After a crash, the next run cannot determine which target owned a stage file; a prefix sweep can delete a legitimate user file with that name or an active stage belonging to another concurrent transfer.
findings.better_approach: Persist exact stage-to-target ownership under a per-session lock or lease and reap only stages whose owner is provably dead; until then, never delete files merely because their names match the prefix.

findings.title: Unbounded concurrent staging can create avoidable disk-full aborts
findings.evidence: docs/plan/SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT.md:593 — the plan acknowledges staging space is the sum of all in-flight records, then explicitly declines admission control at lines 600-603.
findings.predicted_failure: A destination with enough free space to replace each file sequentially but not enough for all worker stages simultaneously can hit ENOSPC and abort the whole session, although throttling staging concurrency would let the transfer complete.
findings.better_approach: Introduce an internal destination-scoped weighted staging budget derived from record sizes and available space, reducing concurrency under pressure without adding a CLI option; test the case where one stage fits but the concurrent sum does not.

findings.title: Pre-creating the staging file disables the APFS clone fast path
findings.evidence: docs/plan/SOURCE_SIDE_CONTAINMENT.md:584 — every stage is created with `create_new`, while the same plan proposes `fclonefileat` at line 388; crates/blit-core/src/copy/file_copy/mod.rs:99 documents that the macOS clone operation requires a nonexistent destination and otherwise always returns EEXIST.
findings.predicted_failure: Every staged local APFS copy falls through from the constant-time clone path to fcopyfile or buffered copying, producing a large systematic throughput and I/O regression and failing the plan's A17 FAST criterion.
findings.better_approach: For macOS local copies, choose a unique absent stage path and invoke `fclonefileat` directly, retrying name collisions; create the stage file only when falling back to fcopyfile or buffered I/O.
